# How to Sell Used Cars Online: A Dealer’s First Week on OPENLANE


[Dealer Operations](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/dealer-operations/) |[Wholesale Strategy](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/wholesale-strategy/) |


- [Selling](https://www.openlane.com/insights/tag/selling/)


4 mins


Sep 23, 2026


Every vehicle on your lot should have a purpose. Some are ready for retail. Others may require too much reconditioning, appeal to a different market or simply no longer justify the space and capital they consume.


That’s where a consistent strategy for selling used cars online can help.


OPENLANE is a digital wholesale marketplace for dealers that gives you a way to expose fresh trades and aged inventory to a local and nationwide network of buyers. If you’re new to selling on the marketplace, the goal of your first week is not to list everything at once. It’s to build a process that helps you identify the right vehicles, present them transparently and make informed selling decisions.


Here’s how to get started:


## How to Wholesale Vehicles for Dealerships: Start With a Clear Goal


Before choosing which vehicles to list, decide what you want wholesale to accomplish when you sell used cars online.


You may need to:


- Move fresh trades that do not fit your retail strategy.
- Reduce[aged inventory](https://www.openlane.com/insights/smarter-aged-inventory-management-for-used-car-dealers/) .
- Avoid taking on a costly reconditioning project.
- Free up capital or floorplan capacity.
- Make room for vehicles that better match local demand.


Knowing the reason behind the sale can help you make better decisions later. A unit that needs to move quickly may require a different pricing strategy than one you are willing to hold a little longer.


Start with a small group of vehicles tied to a clear business objective. That gives your team an opportunity to learn the OPENLANE selling process while producing results you can evaluate.


## Make Transparency Part of Your Selling Strategy


Online wholesale buyers cannot walk around the vehicle or take it for a test drive. They rely on the listing and Condition Reports to understand what they are considering.


You can use the[OPENLANE app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.backlotcars.backlotcars&hl=en_US) to request an inspection at your dealership. Before the inspector arrives, make sure each vehicle is accessible, starts and has its available keys and relevant information ready. You should also identify known cosmetic or mechanical issues.


OPENLANE combines experienced human inspectors with AI-enhanced condition insights. Depending on the vehicle and listing, its[condition report](https://www.openlane.com/insights/condition-reports-your-roadmap-to-faster-and-easier-buying/) may include:


- Inspector observations and test-drive notes
- Exterior damage highlighted
- Engine Audio Analysis that identifies potential noise anomalies
- Plain-language information from the Intelligent OBD2 Decoder
- More than 25 vehicle photos
- Exterior, interior, tire and frame details


These detailed condition reports do more than document a vehicle. They help buyers evaluate potential reconditioning needs, establish a bidding limit and participate with greater confidence.


For sellers, that transparency can help attract serious buyers and set clearer expectations before the sale, reducing the risk of arbitration.


## Let the Vehicle and Your Timeline Guide the Price


Effective wholesale pricing is not just about reaching the highest possible number. It is about balancing potential earnings with time, depreciation, carrying costs and the vehicle’s role on your lot.


OPENLANE Predictive Pricing provides VIN-specific guidance informed by the vehicle’s specifications, condition, current market data and similar sales on OPENLANE. It includes an estimated current value and 30, 60 and 90 day pricing outlooks.


Before setting your price, consider:


- How long the vehicle has been on your lot
- What it costs your dealership to continue holding it
- Whether additional reconditioning would improve its return
- How its value may change over the coming months
- How quickly you want to convert it into working capital


A realistic price can help create buyer interest while supporting the business goal that prompted you to wholesale in the first place.


## Choose a Selling Format That Matches Your Goal


Not every vehicle needs the same path to sale. OPENLANE offers different formats so you can align the listing with your desired outcome.


A **Buy it Now** format gives buyers a clear opportunity to purchase the vehicle immediately. Auction listings let buyers compete through bidding to determine the vehicle’s value.


When certainty and speed are priorities, you can use **Absolute Sale** to commit the vehicle to the highest bidder at the end of the day. **Automated Absolute Sale** can take that strategy one step further by triggering an Absolute Sale once bidding reaches a target price you have established. Learn more about the differences between Absolute Sale and Automated Absolute Sale[here](https://www.openlane.com/insights/when-to-use-absolute-sale-and-automated-absolute-sale-on-openlane/) .


Your OPENLANE rep can help evaluate which approach best fits the vehicle and your dealership’s timeline.


## Turn the First Sale Into a Consistent Process


After your first vehicles move through the marketplace, review the results with your team.


Look at what inventory attracted buyer interest, how your pricing compared with bidding activity and how quickly each vehicle sold. Use what you learned to create a regular process for identifying future wholesale candidates.


That process might begin when a trade is appraised, when a vehicle reaches a defined age or when estimated reconditioning costs exceed your store’s threshold. Set a clear wholesale strategy in advance—for example, identify which vehicles to wholesale based on age in inventory, price point, brand, condition, or expected reconditioning costs. This makes wholesaling a deliberate inventory decision rather than a last resort.


With local and nationwide marketplace access, detailed Condition Reports and forward-looking pricing insights, OPENLANE is a digital wholesale marketplace for dealers specializing in selling used cars online to help move vehicles that no longer fit and make room for inventory that does.

## Frequently Asked Questions From New OPENLANE Sellers


### ***Which vehicles should I consider selling on OPENLANE?***


Potential candidates include fresh trades that do not fit your retail strategy, aged vehicles, units with significant reconditioning needs and inventory that may appeal to buyers outside your local market.


### ***How is the vehicle listing created?***


Dealers can use the OPENLANE US app to request an inspection. An inspector visits your dealership to assess the vehicle and collect the photos, observations and other information used to create its Condition Report and marketplace listing.


### ***How can I decide what price to set?***


Start with your desired selling timeline, carrying costs and the vehicle’s condition. OPENLANE Predictive Pricing can provide additional VIN-specific guidance, including an estimated current value and 30, 60 and 90 day pricing outlooks.


### ***Can I buy and sell through OPENLANE?***


Yes. OPENLANE is a two-sided digital wholesale marketplace connecting dealership buyers and sellers. Dealers can use the platform to both acquire inventory and sell vehicles that no longer fit their retail strategy. Learn more about buying on OPENLANE[here](https://www.openlane.com/insights/how-to-master-your-first-week-buying-on-openlane/) .
